newsitem.title: POLAND: Merrill Lynch retains Okocim neutral rate.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch retains Okocim neutral rate.

text.p: Merrill Lynch maintained its neutral stance on Polish brewer Okocim SA saying the company was fairly valued.
Merrill Lynch said in its December 18 Eastern European roundup it saw Okocim trading at 11.0 times earnings in 1997, down from 11.3 forecast for 1996 and 13.6 in 1995.
"Okocim trading on P/E (97E) of 11.0 and facing declining earnings growth, appears fully valued," it said.
The removal of tariff protection in 1999 could have a negative impact on all breweries including Okocim, it said.
It said that despite summer production hitting capacity restraints sales volume was likely to increase eight percent, while diluted earnings growth was expected at 20.5 percent.

It said however it saw Okocim's earnings growing by only 2.3 percent next year because of higher depreciation charges resulting from an increase in investment and a further squeeze on margins from increasing competition.
It said South African Breweries' (SAB) acquisition of Tychy and Lech made it a very strong local competitor with a 20-percent market share and aggressive pricing.
Last year Okocim had a pre-tax profit of 26.5 million zlotys. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
